The Mimi neural audio codec operates with a sampling frequency of 24kHz and a frame rate of 12.5 frames per second [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 3.3, p. 10]. This is also confirmed in the audio quality evaluation table, which lists the sample rate ($f_s$) as 24kHz and the codec frame rate ($f_r$) as 12.5Hz for the Mimi variants [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 5.2, p. 23].

The objective of the ratio loss is to guide the model toward the desired compression ratio while preserving content-adaptive compression, ensuring the model learns which vectors to retain based on semantic importance rather than following predetermined patterns [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 2.2.3 Ratio Loss, p. 8].

Based on Table 4 in the Moshi paper, Mimi (specifically the variant with adversarial loss only) achieves a subjective MUSHRA quality score of **81.0±1.3**, whereas the RVQGAN baseline achieves a score of **31.3±1.3** [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 5.2 Audio Tokenization, p. 23]. The text further states that Mimi "significantly outperforms RVQGAN" [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 5.2 Audio Tokenization, p. 24].

Based on the provided passages, the **Inner Monologue** in Moshi functions as a mechanism that enables the design of **streaming Text-to-Speech (TTS)** and **streaming Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)** systems by adjusting the delay between text and audio tokens [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 7 Conclusion, p. 41].

The delay relative to user audio (or text, depending on the task) is used to provide **lookahead** or allow the model to **listen to content before generating** the other modality:
*   For **streaming TTS**, audio tokens are delayed by 2 seconds to give the text tokens lookahead [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 5.7 Streaming ASR and TTS, p. 31].
*   For **streaming ASR**, text tokens are delayed by 2 seconds, allowing the model to listen to the audio content before generating text tokens [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 5.7 Streaming ASR and TTS, p. 31].
